blocks.text: Scan scope allows you to select specific DLP engines that must be used to detect and classify sensitive data in specific file types. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is used to scan and identify sensitive data in image files and also images embedded within files. DSPM uses only the specified DLP engines to scan the resources for sensitive data.
To create a new scan scope:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Scan Settings.
Select the Scan Scope tab.
On the Scan Scope page, click Add Scan Scope.
See image.
On the General Information page:
Engine Scope Name: Enter a descriptive name for your scan scope.
Engine Scope Description: Provide a detailed explanation of what the scan scope covers.
See image.
Click Next.
On the Select Criteria page:
DLP Engine: Choose DLP engines for the scan scope. Choose All or Specific DLP Engines.
When you select the Specific DLP Engines option, choose the DLP engines from the list that must be included in the scan scope. To learn more, see About Data Classification Settings.
A DLP engine must be enabled so you can select it while configuring the scan scope. A DLP engine that is not enabled appears grayed out and cannot be selected.

If you disable a DLP engine that is currently selected in a scan scope, it is displayed as grayed out with a partial selection indicator. The scanner does not evaluate this DLP engine, even if it is still partially selected.
When a DLP engine is deleted, it is automatically removed from all existing scan scopes.
File Type: Choose the file types that must be included in the scan scope.
DSPM uses OCR to scan and identify sensitive data in image files (e.g., .png, .jpeg, .tiff, .bmp, .gif) and also images that are embedded within documents (e.g., .pdf, .docx, .pptx).
Machine Learning Document Scan: Enable if you want to use machine learning-powered document scanning.
File type filters, and machine learning document scans are optimized for cloud storage and VM resources.
See image.
Click Next.
On the Summary page, review the configured details. Click the Edit icon to modify the scan scope, if required. To learn more, see Editing or Deleting Scan Scopes.
See image.
Click Finish.

blocks.text: After creating a scan scope, you can apply the scan scope while configuring a scan rule. To learn more, see About Scan Settings.
